section: 4. tools: built-in, in your process, or an outside mcp server
text: Tools: built-in, in your process, or an outside MCP server A tool reaches the model from one of three places, and where it runs decides what it can touch and how it fails: Kind How you add it Where it runs Name the model sees Built-in tools=["Read", "Edit", "Bash"] (or the default set) Inside the Claude Code process, with Claude Code's limits (the Read cap, the Bash output cap: see Claude Code, taken apart , section Tools) Read In-process (SDK MCP server) @tool functions wrapped by create_sdk_mcp_server("repo", tools=[...]) , passed in mcp_servers In your process: the Claude Code process sends each call to you as an mcp_message on the pipe mcp__repo__read_file Outside MCP server mcp_servers={"gh": {"type": "stdio", "command": ...}} or {"type": "http", "url": ...} , or a project .mcp.json A separate process or a remote service that Claude Code connects to mcp__gh__... @tool("read_file", "Return the text of one file.", {"path": str}) async def read_file(args): return {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": open(args["path"]).read()[:20000]}]} repo = create_sdk_mcp_server("repo", tools=[list_files, read_file, edit_file, run_tests]) options = ClaudeAgentOptions(mcp_servers={"repo": repo}, tools=[], ...) What happens on the wire (run s1) MEASURED : before the first model call the Claude Code process opened our server with an MCP initialize (protocol version 2025-11-25, client name claude-code ), sent the initialized notification and asked for tools/list ; the SDK had turned {"path": str} into the JSON schema {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["path"]} .

section: 5. permissions and hooks: your code in the decision
text: The SDK docs give the order: (1) hooks , (2) deny rules ("even in bypassPermissions mode"), (3) ask rules (these go to your callback even in bypass mode), (4) the permission mode , (5) allow rules (including calls a tool approves on its own, such as reading a file in the working directory), (6) your can_use_tool callback ; in dontAsk mode step 6 is skipped and the call is denied ( configure permissions ) DOCS .
label: core

section: 5. permissions and hooks: your code in the decision
text: Two consequences: "Auto-approved tools never reach canUseTool ", so a callback is not an audit log (use a PreToolUse hook for that); and a hook that returns allow still cannot override a deny rule.
label: core

section: 5. permissions and hooks: your code in the decision
text: The SDK source adds that a PreToolUse hook returning allow "also skips" the callback, and setting can_use_tool makes the SDK pass --permission-prompt-tool stdio so the questions come down the pipe SOURCE . s1: hook + callback s2: callback says no s3: nobody answers One step per tool call, in the order the model made them, from the three recordings.
label: core

section: 5. permissions and hooks: your code in the decision
text: The stage that settled each call is read from the recording (hook output, callback log, refusal text); stages before it were passed, stages after it never ran. s1 and s2 use our four tools with a hook that allows the two read-only tools; s3 uses Claude Code's built-in tools with no hook and no callback.

section: 10. deployment, authentication, and the alternatives
text: Because "One agent session maps to one subprocess" that "owns a shell, a working directory, and session files on disk", the hosting page lists four patterns ( hosting ) DOCS : Pattern Shape Fits Ephemeral A container per task, destroyed at the end "bug investigation and fix, invoice and receipt extraction, document translation" Long-running Persistent containers, often several SDK processes each email agents, chat bots, per-user site builders Hybrid Ephemeral containers that load the session from a SessionStore and write it back ("the store is required") conversations that sit idle between turns Multi-agent container Several SDK processes in one container agents that must collaborate closely Sizing starts at "1 GiB RAM, 5 GiB disk, and 1 CPU per agent"; a small container costs "roughly $0.05 per hour, while a single long agent session can spend dollars in tokens"; pin a session to one container by hashing its id; the subprocess needs outbound HTTPS to the API and "does not listen on the network".
